question: What is the main job of foetal circulation?

options.A: To supply oxygen and nutrients from the mother
options.B: To pump blood directly into the mother's kidneys
options.C: To circulate air through the baby's developing lungs
options.D: To filter all waste through the baby's own kidneys

explanation: You've got this! Since a baby in the womb cannot breathe air or eat food yet, the placenta steps in to bring oxygen and nutrients straight from the mother's blood. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Why does blood mostly bypass a baby's lungs before birth?

options.A: The lungs are filled with fluid and not yet used for breathing
options.B: The lungs are too small to hold any blood at all
options.C: Blood cannot reach the upper chest before birth
options.D: Oxygen is produced directly inside the lung tissue

explanation: Great thinking! Foetal lungs are full of amniotic fluid and don't do breathing work yet, so the body routes most of the blood around them. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Which special opening connects the right atrium directly to the left atrium in a foetus?
explanation: Spot on! The foramen ovale is a clever little flap between the upper heart chambers that lets blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: What is the main job of the ductus arteriosus?

options.A: It carries waste products away from the liver
options.B: It pumps blood from the left ventricle to the brain
options.C: It connects the umbilical cord directly to the placenta
options.D: It directs blood from the pulmonary artery into the aorta

explanation: You're doing great! The ductus arteriosus acts as a bridge from the pulmonary artery straight to the aorta, helping blood bypass the resting lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: Which blood vessel carries oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the baby?
explanation: Remember, veins usually carry deoxygenated blood, but the umbilical vein is the special exception—it brings fresh, oxygenated goodness from the placenta to the baby! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: After leaving the baby's heart, where does the freshest, most oxygen-rich blood go first?
explanation: That makes total sense when you think about it: the brain and head need top priority for oxygen to grow rapidly during pregnancy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: Which blood vessels carry used, deoxygenated blood away from the baby back to the placenta?
explanation: You've got this! Two umbilical arteries take the baby's waste products and deoxygenated blood right back to the placenta to be cleaned by the mother's system. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: Where does most of the blood from the baby's right ventricle go?

options.A: Through the ductus venosus into the liver tissue
options.B: Directly into the tiny capillary beds of the lungs
options.C: Through the ductus arteriosus into the aorta
options.D: Straight into the left atrium through the foramen ovale

explanation: Since the lungs are full of fluid and tough to flow through, the blood takes the easy shortcut through the ductus arteriosus straight into the aorta. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: Why do foetal lungs get only a tiny fraction of the body's blood supply?

options.A: They are completely absent during the first two trimesters
options.B: They are blocked by the growing liver tissue
options.C: They are filled with fluid and have high resistance
options.D: They receive all their oxygen directly from the mother's skin

explanation: Uninflated lungs full of amniotic fluid naturally push back against blood flow, so most blood finds easier alternate routes. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: What is the role of the ductus venosus in the baby's abdomen?

options.A: It filters all waste products out of the liver cells
options.B: It supplies the liver with all the baby's red blood cells
options.C: It pumps bile directly from the liver into the umbilical cord
options.D: It allows most oxygenated blood to bypass the liver's capillaries

explanation: Think of the ductus venosus as a VIP bypass lane around the liver, rushing rich oxygen straight to the heart without getting slowed down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: What happens to the baby's blood pressure right after the umbilical cord is clamped?
explanation: You're doing awesome! Cutting the cord removes the low-resistance placenta, which causes an immediate rise in the baby's blood pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)

question: What causes the blood vessels in a newborn's lungs to relax and open up at birth?

options.A: Expansion of the lungs with air and a rise in oxygen
options.B: An increase in pressure from the clamped umbilical cord
options.C: The sudden drop in body temperature outside the womb
options.D: The release of digestive enzymes into the bloodstream

explanation: When the baby takes that magical first breath, the rush of oxygen tells the lung blood vessels to relax and open wide for business! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)

question: What makes the foramen ovale snap shut at birth?

options.A: Higher pressure in the left atrium compared to the right atrium
options.B: The physical tie placed on the umbilical cord
options.C: Contraction of the heart muscle due to cold air
options.D: A sudden drop in the baby's core body temperature

explanation: As blood floods back from the newly working lungs into the left side of the heart, the pressure pushes the little flap of the foramen ovale shut. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: Which temporary foetal structure turns into the ligamentum arteriosum after birth?
explanation: Spot on! Once the ductus arteriosus finishes its job and seals up with high oxygen levels, it turns into a sturdy little ligament called the ligamentum arteriosum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: What is it called when the ductus arteriosus fails to close normally after a baby is born?
explanation: You've got this! 'Patent' simply means open. If that little bypass tube stays open past the newborn period, we call it a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)

question: Which sign is a nurse most likely to notice in a newborn with an open heart shunt like PDA?

options.A: High fever accompanied by generalized body rash
options.B: Extreme weight gain within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: An abnormal heart murmur and breathing difficulty
options.D: Complete inability to pass any meconium stool

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood swirling through unclosed shunts creates extra sounds we hear as a murmur, and extra fluid can make the baby breathe a bit faster. You're learning real clinical skills! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)
